theory.intro: A three-dimensional problem is solved by finding the right-angled triangles hidden inside it. Solve one triangle first to get a length shared with a second triangle. Then use that shared length in the second triangle.
facts: A 3D problem contains two or more triangles lying in different planes: a horizontal base, a vertical slice, or an inclined face.
The two triangles are linked by a **shared edge**, such as a vertical height or a distance across the ground.
Keep each intermediate length in exact form, such as $h = 30\tan 75^{\circ}$ or a surd, so no rounding error builds up.

Three-figure true bearings such as $065^{\circ}\text{T}$ and $155^{\circ}\text{T}$ fix directions in the horizontal plane, and the angle between them is their positive difference, $155^{\circ} - 65^{\circ} = 90^{\circ}$.
steps: Identify and sketch the separate 2D triangles located in the different planes of the 3D figure
Use trigonometry or Pythagoras' theorem in the first triangle to express the shared connecting edge in exact form
Substitute the connecting edge into the second triangle and solve for the required distance, height, or angle
Evaluate the final result and round to the specified degree of accuracy

foundation.question_text:
A vertical antenna $OT$ is supported by two cables anchored at ground points $A$ and $B$.
Cable $AT$ has length $35\text{ m}$ and meets the ground at an angle of elevation of $44^{\circ}$.
Point $B$ is on level ground $22\text{ m}$ from base $O$.
Calculate the angle of elevation $\theta$ of the top of the antenna from point $B$, correct to the nearest degree.

A vertical communications tower $OT$ of height $120\text{ m}$ stands on flat ground.
An observer at point $P$, due south of the tower, measures the angle of elevation to the top $T$ as $32^{\circ}$.
A second observer at point $Q$, due east of the tower, measures the angle of elevation to $T$ as $40^{\circ}$.
Calculate the ground distance $PQ$ between the observers, correct to the nearest metre.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOP\text{:}$
$OP = \frac{120}{\tan 32^{\circ}}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOQ\text{:}$
$OQ = \frac{120}{\tan 40^{\circ}}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta POQ\text{ (south and east meet at }90^{\circ}\text{):}$
$PQ = \sqrt{OP^{2} + OQ^{2}}$
$= \sqrt{\left(\frac{120}{\tan 32^{\circ}}\right)^{2} + \left(\frac{120}{\tan 40^{\circ}}\right)^{2}}$
$= \sqrt{36879.40\dots + 20451.97\dots}$
$= 239.439\dots\text{ m}$
$= 239\text{ m}$

$\text{Distance from base centre }O\text{ to midpoint }M\text{:}$
$OM = \frac{14}{2} = 7\text{ cm}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOM\text{:}$
$\tan\theta = \frac{OT}{OM}$
$= \frac{10}{7}$
$\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{10}{7}\right)$
$= 55.007\dots^{\circ}$
$= 55.0^{\circ}$

foundation.question_text:
A vertical lookout tower $OT$ of height $45\text{ m}$ stands on level ground.
From base $O$, ranger station $A$ is on a bearing of $050^{\circ}\text{T}$ with an angle of elevation to $T$ of $28^{\circ}$, and ranger station $B$ is on a bearing of $140^{\circ}\text{T}$ with an angle of elevation to $T$ of $36^{\circ}$.
Calculate the distance between stations $A$ and $B$, correct to the nearest metre.
foundation.solution_text:
$\angle AOB = 140^{\circ} - 50^{\circ} = 90^{\circ}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOA\text{:}$
$OA = \frac{45}{\tan 28^{\circ}}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOB\text{:}$
$OB = \frac{45}{\tan 36^{\circ}}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta AOB\text{:}$
$AB = \sqrt{OA^{2} + OB^{2}}$
$= \sqrt{\left(\frac{45}{\tan 28^{\circ}}\right)^{2} + \left(\frac{45}{\tan 36^{\circ}}\right)^{2}}$
$= \sqrt{7161.42\dots + 3838.74\dots}$
$= 104.881\dots\text{ m}$
$= 105\text{ m}$

foundation.question_text:
From a point $X$ due south of a flagpole, the angle of elevation of the top is $42^{\circ}$.
From a point $Y$ due east of the flagpole, the angle of elevation of the top is $33^{\circ}$.
If the distance between $X$ and $Y$ along the ground is $85\text{ m}$, calculate the height $h$ of the flagpole, correct to the nearest metre.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Let the base of the flagpole be }F\text{.}$
$FX = \frac{h}{\tan 42^{\circ}}$
$FY = \frac{h}{\tan 33^{\circ}}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta XFY\text{ (south and east meet at }90^{\circ}\text{):}$
$FX^{2} + FY^{2} = 85^{2}$
$h^{2}\left(\frac{1}{\tan^{2} 42^{\circ}} + \frac{1}{\tan^{2} 33^{\circ}}\right) = 7225$
$h = \frac{85}{\sqrt{\cot^{2} 42^{\circ} + \cot^{2} 33^{\circ}}}$
$= \frac{85}{\sqrt{1.2327\dots + 2.3687\dots}}$
$= \frac{85}{\sqrt{3.6015\dots}}$
$= 44.790\dots\text{ m}$
$= 45\text{ m}$

foundation.question_text:
A right pyramid has a square base $ABCD$ of side length $16\text{ cm}$ and slant edge length $VA = 15\text{ cm}$.
Find the angle $\alpha$ that slant edge $VA$ makes with the base plane $ABCD$, correct to the nearest degree.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{In the base square }ABCD\text{ with centre }O\text{:}$
$AC = \sqrt{16^{2} + 16^{2}} = 16\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$
$OA = \frac{16\sqrt{2}}{2} = 8\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta VOA\text{:}$
$\cos\alpha = \frac{OA}{VA}$
$= \frac{8\sqrt{2}}{15}$
$\alpha = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{15}\right)$
$= 41.048\dots^{\circ}$
$= 41^{\circ}$

development.question_text:
Two ground points $P$ and $Q$ lie due south and due west respectively of a vertical cliff of height $60\text{ m}$.
From $P$, the angle of elevation to the top of the cliff is $24^{\circ}$.
From $Q$, the angle of elevation is $19^{\circ}$.
Calculate the distance between $P$ and $Q$, correct to the nearest metre.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Let the base of the cliff be }O\text{.}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOP\text{:}$
$OP = \frac{60}{\tan 24^{\circ}}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOQ\text{:}$
$OQ = \frac{60}{\tan 19^{\circ}}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta POQ\text{:}$
$PQ = \sqrt{OP^{2} + OQ^{2}}$
$= \sqrt{\left(\frac{60}{\tan 24^{\circ}}\right)^{2} + \left(\frac{60}{\tan 19^{\circ}}\right)^{2}}$
$= \sqrt{18167.33\dots + 30379.79\dots}$
$= 220.334\dots\text{ m}$
$= 220\text{ m}$

$\text{In right-angled }\Delta BCG\text{ (face diagonal }BG\text{):}$
$BG = \sqrt{5^{2} + 9^{2}}$
$= \sqrt{25 + 81} = \sqrt{106}\text{ cm}$
$\text{Since }AB\text{ is perpendicular to face }BCGF\text{, }\Delta ABG\text{ is right-angled at }B\text{:}$
$\tan\beta = \frac{AB}{BG}$
$= \frac{12}{\sqrt{106}}$
$\beta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{12}{\sqrt{106}}\right)$
$= 49.379\dots^{\circ}$
$= 49.4^{\circ}$

development.question_text:
A lighthouse $OT$ stands $75\text{ m}$ above sea level.
From ship $X$, the lighthouse has a bearing of $035^{\circ}\text{T}$ and an angle of elevation of $16^{\circ}$.
From ship $Y$, the lighthouse has a bearing of $305^{\circ}\text{T}$ and an angle of elevation of $22^{\circ}$.
Calculate the distance between the two ships, correct to the nearest metre.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Angle subtended at lighthouse base }O\text{:}$
$\angle XOY = (360^{\circ} - 305^{\circ}) + 35^{\circ} = 90^{\circ}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOX\text{:}$
$OX = \frac{75}{\tan 16^{\circ}}$
$OY = \frac{75}{\tan 22^{\circ}}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta XOY\text{:}$
$XY = \sqrt{OX^{2} + OY^{2}}$
$= \sqrt{\left(\frac{75}{\tan 16^{\circ}}\right)^{2} + \left(\frac{75}{\tan 22^{\circ}}\right)^{2}}$
$= \sqrt{68339.73\dots + 34427.68\dots}$
$= 320.573\dots\text{ m}$
$= 321\text{ m}$

development.question_text:
A vertical tent pole $OT$ is anchored by two guy ropes $TA$ and $TB$ attached to the ground.
Guy rope $TA$ is $4.8\text{ m}$ long and makes an angle of $52^{\circ}$ with the ground.
Peg $B$ is located $3.2\text{ m}$ from the base $O$, and $\angle AOB = 90^{\circ}$.
Find the distance $AB$ between the two ground pegs, correct to 2 decimal places.
development.solution_text:
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOA\text{:}$
$OA = 4.8\cos 52^{\circ}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta AOB\text{:}$
$AB = \sqrt{OA^{2} + OB^{2}}$
$= \sqrt{(4.8\cos 52^{\circ})^{2} + 3.2^{2}}$
$= \sqrt{8.7303\dots + 10.24}$
$= \sqrt{18.9703\dots}$
$= 4.355\dots\text{ m}$
$= 4.36\text{ m}$

$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TFA\text{:}$
$FA = \frac{h}{\tan 20^{\circ}}$
$FB = \frac{h}{\tan 15^{\circ}}$
$\text{Since }A\text{ is south of }F\text{ and }B\text{ is east of }A\text{, }\Delta FAB\text{ is right-angled at }A\text{:}$
$FB^{2} = FA^{2} + AB^{2}$
$\left(\frac{h}{\tan 15^{\circ}}\right)^{2} = \left(\frac{h}{\tan 20^{\circ}}\right)^{2} + 50^{2}$
$h^{2}\left(\cot^{2} 15^{\circ} - \cot^{2} 20^{\circ}\right) = 2500$
$h = \frac{50}{\sqrt{\cot^{2} 15^{\circ} - \cot^{2} 20^{\circ}}}$
$= \frac{50}{\sqrt{13.9282\dots - 7.5487\dots}}$
$= \frac{50}{\sqrt{6.3795\dots}}$
$= 19.795\dots\text{ m}$
$= 20\text{ m}$

development.question_text:
A right pyramid has a rectangular base $ABCD$ with $AB = 18\text{ cm}$ and $BC = 10\text{ cm}$.
The perpendicular height of the pyramid is $12\text{ cm}$.
Calculate the angle of inclination of slant edge $VA$ to the base plane, correct to the nearest degree.
development.solution_text:
$\text{In base rectangle }ABCD\text{ with centre }O\text{:}$
$AC = \sqrt{18^{2} + 10^{2}} = \sqrt{324 + 100} = \sqrt{424}\text{ cm}$
$OA = \frac{\sqrt{424}}{2} = \sqrt{106}\text{ cm}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta VOA\text{:}$
$\tan\theta = \frac{VO}{OA}$
$= \frac{12}{\sqrt{106}}$
$\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{12}{\sqrt{106}}\right)$
$= 49.379\dots^{\circ}$
$= 49^{\circ}$

development.question_text:
Two points $A$ and $B$ lie on level ground on opposite sides of a vertical mast $OT$.
From point $A$, the angle of elevation to $T$ is $38^{\circ}$, and the distance $AT$ along the line of sight is $40\text{ m}$.
If the ground distance between $A$ and $B$ is $70\text{ m}$ and points $A, O, B$ lie in a straight line, find the angle of elevation of $T$ from $B$, correct to 1 decimal place.
development.solution_text:
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOA\text{:}$
$OT = 40\sin 38^{\circ}$
$OA = 40\cos 38^{\circ}$
$\text{In line segment }AOB\text{:}$
$OB = 70 - 40\cos 38^{\circ}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOB\text{:}$
$\tan\theta = \frac{40\sin 38^{\circ}}{70 - 40\cos 38^{\circ}}$
$\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{24.6264\dots}{70 - 31.5204\dots}\right)$
$= \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{24.6264\dots}{38.4795\dots}\right)$
$= 32.620\dots^{\circ}$
$= 32.6^{\circ}$

mastery.solution_text:
$FP = h\cot 25^{\circ}$
$FQ = h\cot 18^{\circ}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta PFQ\text{ (south and east meet at }90^{\circ}\text{):}$
$FP^{2} + FQ^{2} = 60^{2}$
$h^{2}(\cot^{2} 25^{\circ} + \cot^{2} 18^{\circ}) = 3600$
$h = \frac{60}{\sqrt{\cot^{2} 25^{\circ} + \cot^{2} 18^{\circ}}}$
$= \frac{60}{\sqrt{4.5989\dots + 9.4721\dots}}$
$= \frac{60}{\sqrt{14.0711\dots}}$
$= 15.995\dots\text{ m}$
$= 16\text{ m}$

mastery.question_text:
From a vertical lighthouse $OT$ of height $80\text{ m}$ above sea level, boat $P$ is observed on a bearing of $060^{\circ}\text{T}$ with an angle of depression of $22^{\circ}$, and boat $Q$ is observed on a bearing of $160^{\circ}\text{T}$ with an angle of depression of $15^{\circ}$.
Calculate the distance between boat $P$ and boat $Q$, correct to the nearest metre.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOP\text{:}$
$OP = \frac{80}{\tan 22^{\circ}} = 198.006\dots\text{ m}$
$\text{In right-angled }\Delta TOQ\text{:}$
$OQ = \frac{80}{\tan 15^{\circ}} = 298.564\dots\text{ m}$
$\text{Angle between bearings in horizontal plane:}$
$\angle POQ = 160^{\circ} - 60^{\circ} = 100^{\circ}$
$\text{By the cosine rule in }\Delta POQ\text{:}$
$PQ^{2} = OP^{2} + OQ^{2} - 2(OP)(OQ)\cos 100^{\circ}$
$= 198.006^{2} + 298.564^{2} - 2(198.006)(298.564)\cos 100^{\circ}$
$= 39206.58 + 89140.54 - (-20524.32)$
$= 148871.44$
$PQ = \sqrt{148871.44} = 385.838\dots\text{ m}$
$= 386\text{ m}$

$\text{In floor rectangle }ABCD\text{:}$
$AC = \sqrt{20^{2} + 15^{2}} = \sqrt{400 + 225} = 25\text{ m}$
$\text{In vertical right-angled }\Delta ACG\text{ with }CG = 6\text{ m}\text{:}$
$\tan\theta = \frac{CG}{AC}$
$= \frac{6}{25} = 0.24$
$\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.24)$
$= 13.495\dots^{\circ}$
$= 13.5^{\circ}$
